applies_why: The judge text weighs the defender's answer to the challenger's Isaiah 8:3-4 bound against the challenger's press on the sign's bounds in DR3's Link 6 footing, which is a collision the rule governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires
room: Whether the Isaiah 8:3-4, 8:8 and 7:16 bounds count as the challenger's own chain (so the rule applies) or as single verses pressed on their own; I read them as part of DR3's Link 6 footing, though the judge's wording treats them verse by verse.
why: The judge resolves the collision by asking whether the sign verse itself states the mechanism, which is the stating-verse test the rule retires, and never weighs the two chains by footing.
